author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This is among the earliest known published writings by Philip K. Dick, printed in his local Berkeley newspaper when he was approximately thirteen years old.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: One of Dick's juvenile publications in his local Berkeley newspaper, printed when he was approximately fifteen years old, alongside 'The Jungle People' (1942) and 'The Visitation' (later in 1944).

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The third known juvenile publication by Dick in his local Berkeley newspaper, following 'The Jungle People' (1942) and 'The Magician's Box' (earlier in 1944).

canonical_title: The Short Happy Life of the Brown Oxford and Other Classic Stories
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Volume 1 of The Collected Stories of Philip K.

canonical_title: The Minority Report and Other Classic Stories
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Volume 4 of The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, this collection gathers short and medium-length fiction written between 1954 and 1964, including previously unpublished pieces, and features an introduction by James Tiptree, Jr.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a future society governed by a game-theory-derived randomization system -- the Quizmaster, the most powerful office in human space, is assigned by a literal, unpredictable lottery designed to prevent any individual or faction from consolidating lasting power, and every citizen is bound by a quasi-feudal 'bottle' contract of near-total obedience to whichever employer holds their service.

canonical_title: Philip K. Dick Reviews Herman Wouk's The Caine Mutiny
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a letter to Time magazine, Dick offered a terse, sardonic one-line verdict on Herman Wouk's bestselling 1951 novel The Caine Mutiny: 'The message I got out of Herman Wouk's Caine Mutiny is (a) Believe! (b) Work! (c) Die!

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a post-nuclear-war society rebuilt around a rigid, puritanical moral code enforced by pervasive surveillance and voluntary neighborhood 'block' informants, Allen Purcell works for an agency producing propaganda that reinforces the state's moral orthodoxy -- until he discovers, to his own horror, that he himself committed an anonymous act of public vandalism against a statue of the movement's revered founder, Major Streiter, apparently while in a dissociated state he cannot fully remember or control.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Ted Barton returns as an adult to his childhood town of Millgate, Virginia, only to find it utterly unrecognizable -- buildings, streets, and even the town's remembered history have been altered, and official records insist he died there as a child years earlier.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Eight visitors touring a Belmont, California particle accelerator (the 'Bevatron') are caught in a radiation accident when the observation platform collapses.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Ragle Gumm lives in a quiet 1950s American town, supporting himself and his sister's family by winning, day after day, a newspaper contest called 'Where Will the Little Green Man Be Next?' His domestic routine -- rivalries with a neighbor, small-town gossip, a crush on the woman next door -- is undercut by a string of accumulating wrongnesses: a soft-drink stand dissolves into a slip of paper reading 'SOFT-DRINK STAND' when Ragle tries to find it; a magazine's celebrity profile describes a person who could not possibly exist; a phone book yields no usable numbers.

canonical_title: The Man in the High Castle
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a world where Nazi Germany and the Japanese Empire won World War II and divided the globe between them, the western United States is under Japanese control (the Pacific States of America), the East is controlled by the Nazis, and a buffer zone of neutral Rocky Mountain States lies between.

author: Philip K. Dick

DICK **THE GAME-PLAYERS OF TITAN** Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Decades after Earth abandoned a psychiatric colony on Alpha III M2, a moon in the Alpha Centauri system, during an interstellar war, the former patients have organized themselves into distinct societal 'clans' each built around a different psychiatric diagnosis -- paranoids running the government and security apparatus, manics providing entrepreneurial energy, obsessive-compulsives handling meticulous bureaucratic administration, hebephrenics forming a religious caste, and so on -- functioning, after generations of self-government, as a stable if eccentric civilization in its own right.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Most of humanity believes World War III is still raging on the surface and has lived for over a decade in vast underground bunkers ('ant tanks'), building robot soldiers called 'leadies' for the war effort while a handful of elite officials -- the Yance-men -- live in comfort on the actual, long-since-peaceful surface, maintaining the fiction of endless war through fabricated newsreels and speeches performed by an aging, ghostwritten figurehead named Talbot Yancy.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a future United States governed as the 'USEA' (United States of Europe and America), the public First Lady, Nicole Thibodeaux, is an eternally youthful media figure adored across generations -- but the presidency itself, 'der Alte,' is in fact a rotating series of android simulacra, and the real power lies with the bureaucratic apparatus that manufactures and stage-manages Nicole's public persona indefinitely across decades.

canonical_title: Dr. Bloodmoney, or How We Got Along After the Bomb
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Before a nuclear war devastates the United States, disgraced physicist Bruno Bluthgeld (who accidentally caused an earlier radiation disaster and believes, with escalating paranoid delusion, that he personally causes catastrophes through the power of his mind) and Walter Dangerfield, a folksy astronaut bound for a Mars colony, are both introduced in Bay Area settings alongside a large ensemble including psychotic TV repairman Stuart McConchie and Hoppy Harrington, a phocomelus (limbless from thalidomide-style birth defects) with latent telekinetic powers.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Earth is a client state of the insectile alien Lilistar in a war against another alien race, the reptilian Reegs, a war Earth is quietly losing and increasingly suspects it should never have joined.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In an overcrowded near-future America grappling with chronic unemployment and racial tension, a repair technician discovers that a malfunctioning experimental Jifi-scuttler (an instantaneous transit device) has opened a permanent crack into a parallel Earth, empty of humans and available for settlement.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a near future where time locally has begun running backward -- the 'Hobart Phase' -- the dead rise from their graves and live their lives in reverse, aging backward toward birth and eventual re-absorption into a mother's womb; the dying gradually revert into infants, and the recently deceased must be dug up ('vitarium' services specialize in this exhumation).

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a Cold War stalemate between the Western bloc ('Wes-bloc') and the Eastern bloc ('Peep-East'), weapons design has become a form of state theater: 'weapons fashion designers' like Lars Powderdry channel psychic trance states to dream up ever more elaborate weapon designs, which are then secretly never built -- both sides have long since agreed, unbeknownst to their populations, to fake an arms race for the sake of domestic morale and economic stimulus while quietly disarming in practice.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Earth has been conquered and occupied for years by the insectile Ganymedeans, who rule through a combination of bureaucratic administration and telepathic-propaganda broadcasts.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In these working notes for 'the Tench novel' -- his working title for A Maze of Death -- Dick sketches a story of an Earth colony on a remote planet undergoing social, economic, and psychological decline, explicitly modeling the decay on Paul Bowles, Kafka's The Castle, and All Quiet on the Western Front's ending ('the last death'), with each colonist decaying by a different characteristic failure mode: alcoholism, schizoid withdrawal ('like me,' Dick notes of himself), flight, and others.

author: Philip K. Dick

canonical_title: The Preserving Machine and Other Stories
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: First published by Ace Books in 1969 and anchored by its title story -- in which a machine transforms musical compositions into living creatures in an attempt to preserve them against a feared future collapse of culture -- this collection showcases Dick's inventive short fiction from the 1950s and 1960s.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Earth is ruled by a rigid biological caste system: a tiny elite of genetically enhanced 'New Men' and telepathic 'Unusuals' govern a vast underclass of ordinary 'Old Men,' whose fitness for even basic civic participation is determined by mandatory aptitude testing rather than any democratic process.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # A Maze of Death *by Philip K.

canonical_title: The Book of Philip K. Dick
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This 1973 collection, dedicated to 'Leslie Busby: the little black-haired girl I love so much,' gathers stories Dick wrote primarily between 1952 and 1955: Nanny, The Turning Wheel, The Defenders, Adjustment Team, Psi-man, The Commuter, A Present for Pat, Breakfast at Twilight, and Shell Game.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Set in Marin County, California, the novel alternates first-person narration between Jack Isidore, a socially maladroit, obsessively literal-minded collector of pseudo-scientific trivia (flying saucers, hollow-earth theories, perpetual motion) who moves in with his sister Fay and her husband Charley after Charley's heart attack, and Fay herself, whose marriage is disintegrating amid infidelity, contempt, and a slow-motion domestic collapse that Jack observes with the same uncomprehending, catalog-minded precision he brings to his pseudo-scientific enthusiasms.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This corpus of 27 letters from Dick to Claudia Bush (later Bush Krenz), spanning January 1975 through March 1979, forms one of the richest interpretive correspondences in the Selected Letters.

canonical_title: Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick, 1975-1976
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This volume continues the Underwood-Miller Selected Letters series, edited by Don Herron with an introduction by Tim Powers -- a close personal friend of Dick's during this period and himself a noted fantasy novelist -- covering Dick's post-2-3-74 years.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: After a nuclear war, a new religion has arisen worshipping Carleton Lufteufel, the scientist responsible for the weapon that devastated civilization, now venerated as the wrathful 'Deus Irae' (God of Wrath) by the Servants of Wrath sect, in uneasy rivalry with a surviving Christian church.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Writing to psychologist Julian Jaynes shortly after reading The Origin of Consciousness in the Breakdown of the Bicameral Mind, Dick offers Jaynes's bicameral-mind theory as the first framework that lets him publicly discuss his March 1974 visionary experience without being dismissed as merely schizophrenic.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Writing to Eugene Warren after returning from a trip to Metz, France -- where he delivered a speech on heavy theology that a local paper reported under the headline 'For Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Dick lays out, in relatively systematic expository prose rather than his Exegesis's usual associative journal style, a private cosmology built around three tiers of reality.

canonical_title: How to Build a Universe That Doesn't Fall Apart Two Days Later
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Opening with a self-deprecating bit about representing Disneyland (he lives nearby, and was once interviewed there while spinning in a teacup ride), Dick lays out what he calls his two lifelong preoccupations as a writer: 'What is reality?' and 'What constitutes the authentic human being?' He traces the first question through his own fiction -- a childhood story about a dog who misreads garbagemen as food thieves, leading him to wonder whether each person inhabits a genuinely private reality, and whether a schizophrenic's reality might be no less real, only incommunicable; and a story about an android (Garson Poole) who discovers his reality is literally recorded on punched tape he can edit.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This is the first half (pages 1 through 5) of a ten-page sequence from Folder 18 of Philip K. Dick's Exegesis, dated August 1978 -- roughly four and a half years after the initial 2-3-74 visionary experiences.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This is the second half (pages 6 through 10) of the same ten-page sequence from Folder 18 of Philip K. Dick's Exegesis continued from the preceding pages 1-5, dated August 1978. No OCR text layer exists for these pages in this corpus, so their specific content cannot be reported.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This 2011 Houghton Mifflin Harcourt omnibus collects Dick's three final novels: VALIS (1981), The Divine Invasion (1982), and The Transmigration of Timothy Archer (1982), together representing his most sustained engagement with theology, Gnosticism, and the nature of divine reality, drawing heavily on his 1974 mystical experiences and Exegesis writings.

canonical_title: Philip K. Dick on Blade Runner
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This Starlog Magazine piece is understood, from its title and byline, to record Dick's own commentary on the Blade Runner film adaptation of Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, made in the period shortly before his death in March 1982.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: An overcrowded Earth is offered emigration to a colony world, Whale's Mouth, reachable only via the one-way instantaneous teleportation service of Trails of Hoffman Limited -- a corporation whose monopoly on the route has driven Rachmael ben Applebaum's family slower-than-light passenger-ship business to ruin.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: An overcrowded, dystopian Earth is offered apparent salvation by Trails of Hoffman Limited, a corporation that instantaneously teleports emigrants to a colony world, Whale's Mouth, advertised as an idyllic new home.

canonical_title: The Mainstream That Through the Ghetto Flows: An Interview with Philip K. Dick
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a wide-ranging, digressive, frequently comic conversation, Dick discusses the arbitrary marketing distinction between 'science fiction' and 'mainstream' fiction (illustrated by the same manuscript being classified differently by Doubleday's hardcover and Ballantine's paperback divisions over the mere presence of profanity), the poor economics of genre publishing (book-club editions that gut royalties, a $6,000 advance from DAW he considers generous), and his own writing history from age twelve through his first sale to Fantasy & Science Fiction in 1951 and his first novel sale, Solar Lottery.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Written in October 1974 -- five years after the novel Ubik's 1969 publication and shortly after Dick's own March 1974 religious experience -- this screenplay reworks the same core story (Glen Runciter's psi-talent security agency, the bombing that leaves the team trapped in an entropically decaying reality, Joe Chip's search for the reality-restoring product Ubik, and the late revelation of who is actually alive and who is not) for the film medium rather than the novel form.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In an alternate United States under the increasingly authoritarian rule of President Ferris F.

canonical_title: The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This is the complete five-volume Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick in a single 2,275-page omnibus, published by Underwood-Miller in 1987 with a preface by Dick himself (drawn from a letter to John Betancourt), a foreword by Steven Owen Godersky, and an introduction by Roger Zelazny.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a small, stifling California town in the 1950s, Mary Anne Reynolds, a young woman working at a record shop, chafes against the narrow social and romantic options available to her -- an unsatisfying engagement, a stagnant hometown, and the expectations of her family -- and becomes entangled in a series of relationships, most significantly with Joseph Schilling, an older, culturally sophisticated record-shop proprietor recently arrived from a bigger city, and with a Black jazz musician, a relationship that draws the period's racial prejudice directly into the novel's small-town social fabric.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: On a future Earth where all cats and dogs have been banned, young Nick Graham and his family emigrate to the distant planet Plowman's Planet so that Nick can keep his cat, Horace.

canonical_title: In Pursuit of VALIS: Selections from the Exegesis
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This 1991 Underwood-Miller anthology, edited by Lawrence Sutin with a preface by Sutin, an introduction by Jay Kinney (Gnosis Magazine's founding editor), an afterword by Terence McKenna, and a PKD chronology by Paul Williams, was the first major published selection from Dick's Exegesis -- his sustained, roughly 8,000-handwritten-page attempt to interpret the visionary experiences he underwent in February and March 1974 ('2-3-74') through theology, Gnostic philosophy, Neoplatonism, and quantum physics.

canonical_title: Second Variety and Other Classic Stories
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A comprehensive, 499-page collection of Dick's short fiction anchored by the title story 'Second Variety,' one of his most celebrated early works about self-replicating war machines.

canonical_title: The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick: 1977-1979
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This volume, edited by Don Herron with an introduction by Robert Anton Wilson -- author of the Illuminatus!

canonical_title: The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick: 1972-1973
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: At 423 pages, this is the largest volume in the Underwood Books Selected Letters series, documenting one of the most turbulent and transformative periods in Dick's life: the mysterious 1971 break-in at his San Rafael home, his 1972 trip to Vancouver for a science fiction convention where he delivered the speech 'The Android and the Human,' his brief sojourn in Canada, a suicide attempt, his entry into the X-Kalay drug rehabilitation program, and his eventual relocation to Orange County, California.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: As the Chinese Communist government prepares to take possession of an American industrial compound in China at the close of the civil war period, three Americans -- Carl Fitter, an older company employee; Verne Tildon, a younger colleague; and Barbara Mahler, a young woman connected to the compound -- remain behind during the final days of the handover, isolated together in a compound emptying of its former life and purpose.

canonical_title: The Shifting Realities of Philip K. Dick: Selected Literary and Philosophical Writings
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Edited by Lawrence Sutin -- author of the definitive Dick biography Divine Invasions and editor of In Pursuit of VALIS -- this is the most comprehensive single-volume gathering of Dick's nonfiction writing: philosophical essays, journal entries, speeches, autobiography, science fiction criticism, and two chapters of a proposed sequel to one of his award-winning novels, alongside provocative essays including 'The Android and the Human' and 'If You Find This World Bad, You Should See Some of the Others.' Sutin's editorial introduction frames Dick as both a brilliant science fiction novelist and a visionary philosopher who chose to couch his speculations in fiction, and the Boston Phoenix praised the collection for unearthing 'gems' for both casual and serious readers.

canonical_title: The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick, Volume 1: 1938–1971
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The first volume of Dick's selected correspondence, covering over three decades from his teenage years through the early 1970s, with an introduction by fantasy novelist James Blaylock, a friend of Dick's writing from personal acquaintance.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Published posthumously in 1997 at 505 pages, this anthology opens with 'Fair Game,' in which an exhausted Colorado professor's ordinary domestic evening is disrupted by hints of government research -- a characteristic Dickian move of beginning with a mundane, recognizable scene before introducing destabilizing elements.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Stuart Hadley, a television-and-appliance salesman in a Bay Area electronics store, feels suffocated by his marriage, his job, and the conformist consumer culture of 1950s suburban California, and drifts through a series of attempted escapes -- an affair, an entanglement with a charismatic Black religious cult leader whose sect offers an alternative community and belief system, and a spiraling personal crisis that estranges him further from his wife and his own sense of purpose.

canonical_title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a San Francisco depopulated by nuclear fallout from World War Terminus, bounty hunter Rick Deckard is assigned to 'retire' six escaped Nexus-6 androids -- the most advanced synthetic humans yet built, nearly indistinguishable from humans except by the Voigt-Kampff empathy test.

canonical_title: A Dark-Haired Girl & PKD: Letters from the Heart, the Spleen, and the Funnybone
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This fifty-one-page collection, compiled and edited by Linda Castellani (Linda Levy) in 2008, presents her personal correspondence with Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This is the second of two Library of America volumes dedicated to Philip K. Dick (following Four Novels of the 1960s, 2007), collecting Martian Time-Slip, Dr. Bloodmoney, Now Wait for Last Year, Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said, and A Scanner Darkly, and edited by Jonathan Lethem.

canonical_title: The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick: 1980-1982
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The final volume in the Selected Letters series, covering the last years of Dick's life, opens with an extraordinary passage in which Dick describes what he calls his 'second theophany' -- which he considered the most treasured moment of his life -- standing in his kitchen with his friend Ray Torrence (referenced in Dick's story 'I Hope I Shall Arrive Soon,' also known as 'Frozen Journey') at about eleven in the morning, as Torrence was about to return to Northern California after staying overnight.

canonical_title: The Exegesis of Philip K. Dick
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This landmark 2011 publication presents an edited and annotated selection from Dick's vast private philosophical journal -- an estimated 8,000 handwritten and typed pages compiled over the final eight years of his life as he attempted to understand the mystical experiences he underwent in February and March 1974 ('2-3-74').

canonical_title: The Second Philip K. Dick MEGAPACK
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Published by Wildside Press in 2015 as part of their popular MEGAPACK e-book series and compiled as a companion to the first Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This is a five-page scanned letter by Dick concerning the craft or practice of writing; the recipient and precise date are unknown, and no OCR text layer exists in this corpus to establish its specific content.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This anthology gathers ten Philip K. Dick short stories published to accompany the Channel 4/Amazon television anthology series Electric Dreams, with each story preceded by an introduction from the episode's screenwriter or producer: Exhibit Piece (Ronald D.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This omnibus volume collects five major Philip K. Dick novels in a single edition. The extracted text opens with A Scanner Darkly (1977), Dick's semi-autobiographical novel about drug addiction and surveillance in a near-future Orange County, whose acknowledgments cite Joseph E.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: These are the opening six handwritten pages of Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A single-page scanned letter by Dick, apparently written in September of an unspecified year; no OCR text layer exists in this corpus, so its recipient and specific content cannot be reported.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A 13-page scanned document containing photocopies of signed letters by Dick; no OCR text layer exists in this corpus, so the number of individual letters, their recipients, dates, and content cannot be reported.

canonical_title: Schizophrenia and the Book of Changes
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Writing for the science fiction fanzine Niekas in 1965, Dick attempts to give the schizophrenic's fearful, isolated perceptual experience an analytical coherence that might extend beyond purely personal pathology into a genuine alternative viewpoint on human experience.

canonical_title: Selected Stories of Philip K. Dick
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: This anthology draws from Dick's prolific short fiction output, primarily written in the 1950s and early 1960s, to present a curated selection of his shorter works.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A twenty-five-chapter outline, headed 'Wanderer Miracle Child Benji' and subtitled 'The Earthshaker,' sketches a mythic-religious narrative in three named stages -- '(Coming),' '(Being),' and an implied '(Resolution & descent?).' A wandering man returns to his village and encounters a miraculous child; he meets Benjie, described as 'the earth woman,' and the two households merge amid vague, unspecified 'change' moving on the road toward them.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A nervous street vendor sells a wind-up toy soldier to a boy named Bobby, unaware — or perhaps all too aware — that the toy is an intelligent, autonomous being executing a plan.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A Martian colony settlement, wary after a prior traveling carnival cheated them, plans to use their psychokinetic boy Fred Costner covertly against a new alien carnival ship's rigged games.

canonical_title: A Little Something for Us Tempunauts
author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: Final Stage, edited by Edward L. Ferman and Barry N. Malzberg, 1974
card_summary: Three American time travelers — Addison Doug, Benz, and Crayne — return from history's first crewed time-travel launch only to learn, via television, that they were killed in an implosion on reentry.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Eric Blake returns from a Ganymede posting and gives his unenthusiastic wife Pat an unusual souvenir: a small, genuinely omnipotent, chronically foul-tempered alien deity, Tinokuknoi Arevulopapo, smuggled illegally to Earth in a box.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A Clerk arrives to make sure a sleepy dog — the neighborhood's Summoner — barks at exactly 8:15 to bring insurance salesman Ed Fletcher 'A Friend with a Car,' getting him to his office an hour early before Sector T137 is taken offline for a scheduled 'adjustment.' The dog oversleeps by one minute.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Five years after a global war, a planet-wide network of automated factories continues to supply human settlements with food and goods, exactly as instructed before the collapse.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: Planet Stories, July 1952 — the first Dick story to appear in print
card_summary: A ship provisioning on Mars takes aboard a wub — an enormous, placid, pig-like animal bought from a native for fifty cents by the crewman Peterson. Captain Franco intends to eat it; the ship's stores have spoiled and there is nothing to feed the crew for a month. The wub then speaks.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Larry gives his wife Doris a hand-made German cuckoo clock, immediately spoiling the gift by mentioning he got it wholesale through a friend.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: The McLean family — Tim, Mary, and their three children — wake to an ordinary foggy morning, only for soldiers in gas masks to smash through their front door moments later.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: Fantasy and Science Fiction, September 1987 (written earlier, unpublished in Dick's lifetime)
card_summary: Cadbury, a discontented beaver in an anthropomorphic animal society run on a poker-chip currency, is nagged by his shrewish wife Hilda into psychiatric treatment with the amiably useless Dr. Drat.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Elderly country storekeeper Edna Berthelson makes a secretive weekly business trip alone in her pickup truck, exploiting an inexplicable personal ability to shift into a branching post-nuclear-war 'ahead' where a small colony of survivors is desperately assembling a salvaged Army rocket to escape a dying, radioactive Earth for Venus.

canonical_title: Chains of Air, Web of Aether
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Leo McVane lives alone in an isolated communications dome on a frozen, double-sunned world, his only real companionship the recorded voice of Linda Fox, a singer who reworks the Elizabethan lute songs of John Dowland for a scattered, exiled human diaspora.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A survey unit has spent three weeks on Planet Blue and found no harmful life form at all — no disease, no vermin, nothing. The place is so unspoiled that one officer has stopped smoking because he cannot bring himself to litter it, and the joke is that it might be Eden.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a sterile, uniform twenty-second century, George Miller curates the Twentieth Century exhibit at the History Agency, immersing himself so completely in his research period — its clothes, slang, briefcase, pipe tobacco — that his colleague Fleming warns him he is becoming a political liability.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, 1953
card_summary: An unnamed man crushes two eavesdropping caterpillars under his foot on his way to the bus, cautiously avoids a spider web, and rides home uneasy about an insect world he half-perceives is aware of him.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Six astronauts crash-land back on Earth after a Mars expedition, jubilant to be home, only to find every town they pass through emptying in silent terror at the sight of them.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Professor Anthony Douglas, a leading nuclear physicist, is terrorized by an enormous eye peering through his window, then by a gigantic cosmic face blotting out the stars.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a Hanoi where the Party has won the global war, Tung Chien is a mid-level functionary at the Ministry of Cultural Artifacts. A legless war-veteran peddler compels him by law to buy a herbal remedy, and sells him what is described as something to rest eyes wearied by official monologues.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: Star Science Fiction Stories No. 3, edited by Frederik Pohl, 1955
card_summary: In a Cold War future organized entirely around the threat of imminent nuclear and bacterial attack, schoolboy Mike Foster is the only child in his class whose family has no private bomb shelter, because his father Bob, a struggling furniture-store owner, is a defiant 'anti-P' who refuses to buy into what he sees as a manufactured, endless arms-race consumer racket.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Jill Herrick is married to Lester, a toxicologist who develops poisons for the military and who treats warmth, metaphor, food and children as forms of imprecision.

canonical_title: I Hope I Shall Arrive Soon
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: On a ten-year interstellar crossing with sixty emigrants in cryonic suspension, one sleeper's tank malfunctions.

canonical_title: If There Were No Benny Cemoli
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A decade after a nuclear war ('the Misfortune') devastated Earth, an armada from the intersystem relief agency CURB finally arrives to oversee reconstruction, to the visible discomfort of the local political leadership who had quietly been governing the ruins themselves.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Spence Olham, a senior researcher on a wartime defense project against the alien Outspacers, is arrested on his morning commute by Major Peters of the security service and his own old friend Nelson, who tell him he is not human at all: an Outspace humanoid robot, containing a U-Bomb triggered by a spoken phrase, sent to kill and replace the real Olham and detonate once inside the Project.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a future Earth rebuilt and ruled entirely by robots after a war destroyed all human institutions and knowledge, humans occupy a strictly segregated underclass — body servants, gardeners, entertainers — barred from governance by 'Lists' (aptitude tests) that, per official history, no human has ever passed, since the tests are designed around robot cognition.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Every few years, dry, cobweb-like Martian creatures ('buggies') drift down to Earth in clouds and are hunted and destroyed by panicked mobs the moment they are spotted.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Historian Hasten is secretly shown a forbidden 'Time Dip' — illegal because observing the future irrevocably alters it — being used by a government research team to photograph conditions decades and centuries ahead. Early results looked utopian: peace, leisure, cities shrinking gracefully.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a future ruled by a small cabal of 'id bloc' industrial leaders who maintain power through an all-female Agency of psychic 'Immune' investigators hunting down parakinetic mutants ('P-K's) -- individuals whose delusions can warp reality around them -- industrialist John Eggerton is targeted by a random loyalty check and flees rather than submit to a mind-probe, terrified of being exposed as P-K himself.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a comfortable future household, a spherical robot Nanny raises the Fields children with total competence — waking them, walking them safely to school, disciplining them with iron patience, protecting them from bullies and drunks.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Obelisk Books, a Martian-colony publisher, discovers that its deluxe hardcover editions — bound in Martian wub-fur, a hide so vital it never fully dies — have been silently rewriting the texts they cover.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a mandatory-attendance communal apartment building, brothers Ian and Al Duncan dream of escaping their cramped, surveilled, bureaucratic lives by performing their amateur 'classical jug' act -- Baroque music played on ceramic jugs -- for Nicole Thibodeaux, the eternally young, universally adored First Lady who has effectively displaced the President as the true object of the one-party society's devotion.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Lemuel, a mutant boy capable of dissecting derelicts and attacking classmates without a flicker of remorse, is committed by his terrified parents to a psychiatric hospital, where Dr.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Lori, a young Boston-raised wife transplanted to rural Vermont, is summoned by a dead leaf tapping at her window, which she tucks against her skin with an almost erotic charge.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Bored military-exemption consultant Jesse Slade visits a time-travel agency, Muse Enterprises, hoping to inspire a great historical figure since he lacks any creative talent of his own.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Peggy Nye spends nearly all her time in her lush garden with Sir Francis, her pet duck, to her husband Robert's mild bemusement.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: After a nuclear war has reduced the world to ash and rubble, human settlements survive by trading their salvaged pre-war goods to the Biltong — alien, amoeba-like creatures drawn to Earth by the H-bomb flashes — who duplicate them.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Psychiatrist Doctor Harris is called in to examine Corporal Westerburg, a healthy young Patrolman stationed at a remote asteroid checkpoint garrison who has calmly declared himself to be a plant and refuses to do anything but sit motionless in the sun.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Three centuries after a war left Earth's surface radioactive, Trent — one of a dwindling colony of unmutated 'true humans' surviving underground in a Pennsylvania mine — treks north in a lead-lined suit searching for other human settlements, since his own colony's failing equipment means extinction is near.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: After six years reconstructing Mars following Terra's defeat in the Prox-Terra war, exhausted reconstruct engineer Milt Biskle asks to go home instead of accepting his reward — priority land on the world he rebuilt.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: With the Terran System Senate on the verge of capitulating to the rebel colony of Ganymede over control of the only deep-space launch cradles, a captured Ganymedean ship — untranslatable, of unknown propulsion — offers a last-minute alternative.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Paul Sharp, an economist at a post-nuclear-war reclamation agency, seeks psychiatric help from Dr. Humphrys for a worsening phobia of heights and falling that has begun crippling his ability to do his job.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Peace officers stop John Cupertino for driving at 160 miles an hour, and find a man in quiet crisis: he insists that his surroundings are unreal, that he can pass his hand through solid objects, and that this all began with the death of his wife Carol — whom he remembers killing on Ganymede three years earlier.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Police officer Joseph Tinbane raids an illegal alien ('outspacer') gambling casino on Terra, watching the alien operators incinerate the entire building — customers, evidence, and all — as their ship departs, exactly as expected.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Boris, a large black dog belonging to the Cardossi family, barks a single word — 'Roog' — at figures nobody else can see. The reader is given the dog's understanding from the first line and never leaves it.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Ed Morris commutes home from Ganymede to Earth through a solar system saturated with advertising — audio and visual ads that fire directly into commuters' brains, salesrobots that swarm pedestrians and cannot be shaken.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Six years into a nuclear war that has left most of the northern hemisphere ash, the American government has withdrawn to a Moon base and left its troops dug into bunkers on a dead Earth.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Paint-company research director David Courtland is interrupted one evening by a nervous young repairman who has arrived to service his 'swibble' — a device Courtland has never heard of.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: An isolated colony of roughly a hundred people on the bog-covered planet Betelgeuse II has spent five years under siege by unseen 'attackers' — gas raids, sabotage, poisoned water — that no one has ever directly seen, defending itself with elaborate paranoid countermeasures (individualized armor, prophylactic capsules, constant surveillance of one another).

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Verne Haskel, exhausted and embittered after twenty resentful years at Larson's Pump and Valve Works, retreats each evening to his basement, where he has spent his entire life building an obsessively exact miniature model of his hometown of Woodland — every store, house and street, down to the display cases in the shop windows.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Bob Clarke is called up for another tour fighting the Martians over rexeroid, a mineral essential to his household's automated control systems, and offers his wife Joan a matter-of-fact economic justification: without rexeroid, kryon, or lonolite, ordinary technological comforts (car steering, climate-controlled walls, computer memory) would collapse.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: After three centuries, the legendary 'lost' Williamson's World — colonized by the first human to leave the Solar System — is finally rediscovered.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: Unpublished in his lifetime; held in the PKD Estate Archives
card_summary: In a future City of Lightness where citizens fly on mechanical wings, Robert Benton is summoned to the Controller's office and told that an invention he has no memory of submitting has been denied: humanity, having reached the absolute limit of its ingenuity a century earlier, adopted 'Stabilization' — a rigidly enforced freeze on all further change, backed by yearly exams, forced disappearances, and a fate called 'the Cart' for those who backslide.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Surveying an uncharted, pristine planet, the cautious Captain Johnson stays with the ship while his brash colleague Brent explores on foot, encountering enormous, docile predator cats and eventually a marble mansion tended by tame, evolving animals.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Dick describes an October morning in his Orange County apartment building, which has been converted to condominiums; he has decided to buy his unit for $52,000 rather than move, while nearly everyone else has already left.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Thirty years into a war that has stripped Earth's surface to ash and driven humanity into underground tunnels, a survey team leaps from a crashing rocket onto Mars, the last untested planet in the solar system, hoping to find a habitable refuge.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: E.J. Elwood, a suburban husband and father, has spent a year building an enormous, purposeless wooden boat in his backyard, working every free hour with the quiet, unquestioning help of his younger son Toddy.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a near-future society polarized entirely into two rigid political factions — the hygiene-obsessed 'Purists,' who demand compulsory grooming and deodorization, and the body-accepting 'Naturalists,' who resist as a matter of principle — ordinary commuter Don Walsh refuses to join either side, insisting the whole conflict is trivial and manufactured.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A tired commuter named Ernest Critchet asks ticket agent Ed Jacobson for a new commute book to a town called Macon Heights.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Overweight, food-obsessed schoolboy Bubber Surle visits an elderly, isolated widow, Mrs. Drew, purely for her fresh-baked cookies, tolerating her requests that he stay and read to her from his schoolbooks as the price of the treat.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A Terran patrol ship spots an armed Adharan freighter illegally trespassing in the closed Sirius system, methodically landing on planet after planet, sending out swarms of crew to gather something unknown, then moving on.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: Fantastic Universe, July 1954 (as "Foundation of Fear" / "The Crawlers")
card_summary: In rural Tennessee, near a radiation lab, government investigator Ernest Gretry examines a mangled, snail-like creature killed on the highway — a mutant child, one of a growing population being born to local families in the wake of radiation exposure.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

canonical_title: The Day Mr. Computer Fell Out of Its Tree
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Joe Contemptible wakes to a world run by a vast central computer that has gone psychotic, dispensing bloomers instead of suits, soap instead of coffee, and a newspaper headlined 'Adolf Hitler Crowned Pope.' The only cure is Ms.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Survivors of a hydrogen war — 'flukers', so named because they lived by a fluke of fate — shelter in underground pits, kept alive by Martian 'careboys' who parachute supplies they no longer need. The pits are full of food.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Eight years into a nuclear war, the entire human population of both blocs lives in sealed installations beneath the surface, manufacturing weapons that robots called leadies carry up and use.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, October 1969
card_summary: Garson Poole wakes in hospital after a crash, missing a right hand and feeling no pain, and is informed by his doctor that he is not a man but an 'electric ant' — an organic robot. The hospital cannot treat him, but bills him for services rendered up to the point of discovery.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Bob Bibleman, a floating-home salesman in a future where robots handle all low-wage work, idly answers a fast-food robot's contest question and wins, at two-trillion-to-one odds, a full scholarship to the College — an elite, unadvertised, military-chartered institution that selects rather than being selected.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Dark Side, edited by Damon Knight, 1976
card_summary: An aging Roman priest named Philos Diktos of Tyana ('Philip' transliterated into Greek and Latin) confesses, near the end of his life, a secret witnessed decades earlier at the temple of the Cumaean Sibyl, shortly after the assassination of Julius Caesar.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: Fantastic Universe, January 1953 (as by Richard Phillips)
card_summary: A man idly reading a paperback novel he found on the bus becomes convinced, sentence by sentence, that he has stumbled onto proof of an alien invasion already living undetected among ordinary people.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, December 1954
card_summary: Eight-year-old Charles Walton is sent to fetch his father for dinner and comes back unable to say which of them to fetch: there are two, and they look alike. The one that comes in to eat is the father-thing.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: If, April 1954 (Quinn Publishing Co.) — byline details confirmed by Dick himself in a 1975 letter to his agent
card_summary: In a post-war America where radiation has produced mutants — 'deeves' — the Department of Civic Anthropology hunts and euthanises them at birth; eighty-seven types have been catalogued and dealt with in sixty years.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Fifty years after 'the Smash,' a post-apocalyptic tribe living in an underground concrete shelter sends a chosen young man, Tim Meredith, on an annual pilgrimage through irradiated ruins to a vast ruined federal research building, where a surviving super-computer called 'the Great C' awaits three carefully-prepared questions.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A survey crew discovers a planet whose entire surface has been reduced to fused slag by nuclear war, and whose ruined city, Franklin Apartments, still guards itself with an automated anti-aircraft gun that shoots down their ship on sight, killing its captain and stranding the survivors.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: TV store owner Ed Loyce drives past his small town's central park one evening and sees a mutilated corpse hanging from the lamppost — and no one else reacts to it at all.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a Free Union government dependent on telepathic mutants ('teeps') born from a nuclear accident to police ideological loyalty, mysterious metal 'hoods' begin circulating that block mind-probes entirely, and anyone caught wearing one is mobbed and stripped of it by a suspicious public egged on by teep agents.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Irma Gordon, a deaf, three-hundred-fifty-year-old woman -- one of the oldest people alive and near the end of her sustained lifespan -- arrives at a spaceport with her robant escort and a fortune in savings, demanding passage to Earth: humanity's legendary birthplace, long since proven by science to be a myth with no verifiable location.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Physics professor Hardy and philosophy professor Grote publicly feud over Zeno's paradox — whether a frog jumping half the remaining distance to the top of a well can ever actually get out — until their exasperated Dean orders them to settle it experimentally.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A small prospecting crew -- Major Crispin Eller, second-in-command Harrison Blake, and lab technician Silvia Simmons -- lands on a barren but perfectly habitable asteroid that inexplicably harbors no life at all, and is struck unconscious by a mysterious pulse of radiation from the asteroid's core.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Shadrach Jones, an old man running a nearly abandoned filling station in Derryville, Colorado, gives shelter one stormy night to a bedraggled party of Elves carrying their dying king on a platform.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Zen Buddhism scholar Joan Hiashi is recruited by the State Department to bring her expertise to Havana, ostensibly to convert wealthy Chinese-Cuban businessmen away from Communism, but really as bait: her lover, jazz harpist and telepath Ray Meritan, is suspected of connections to Mercerism, a new religious movement sweeping the world built around 'empathy boxes' — devices that let followers literally share, in real time, the suffering of Wilbur Mercer as he walks toward his death on an alien world.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: On Callisto, a team of anonymous 'yance-men' produce daily video 'gestalts' of John Edward Yancy, a folksy, avuncular composite personality — homespun wisdom, a devoted grandson, opinions on everything from primroses to just war — broadcast to the entire moon and treated by its population as the most beloved man alive.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, October 1974
card_summary: In a near-future California, Congress has extended abortion law past birth: a child has no soul, and so no legal protection, until it can do algebra — a test the law sets at twelve.

author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, June 1953
card_summary: Doc Labyrinth, convinced that civilisation is going the way of Rome and that a dark age is coming, worries that music is the most perishable of the things that will be lost.

canonical_title: The Short Happy Life Of The Brown Oxford
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Conger, a convicted smuggler and skilled hunter, is offered release from prison by a totalitarian Council in exchange for a mission: travel back in time to twentieth-century Colorado and kill the founder of the pacifist First Church before he ever preaches.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Centuries after an apocalyptic 'Time of Madness,' a rigid caste theocracy governs the survivors, its doctrine of reincarnation administered through a rusting, decaying 'scanner' technology that lets the faithful preview their next incarnation on the cosmic ladder.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a future where a crime is solved by a forensic 'file bank' that narrows the population from billions to a handful of suspects through successive physical specifications, an autonomous watchdog robot — an 'M' (machine), built to hunt poachers on frontier plantations — is diverted by wealthy slaver Paul Tirol to assassinate his own business front man, Heimie Rosenburg, and frame Tirol's business rival, David Lantano, by planting false forensic clues (blood type, hair, a heel print) engineered to point the investigation's ten specifications directly at Lantano.

card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Larry Brewster, drinking alone in a bar, is approached by the poised, unhurried Allison Holmes, who calmly explains a solipsistic philosophy: each person inhabits their own private world in which they alone are wholly real, while everyone else exists only partially, arranged for their happiness.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In a bleak future where surviving humanity toils underground for rigid, bureaucratic Companies that emerged after an obscure war, low-level letter carrier Applequist discovers a damaged, still-conscious android buried in a ravine — the last survivor of a robot civilization officially destroyed and forbidden even to be discussed.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Ten-year-old Tony Rossi, born on the colonized planet of the insectile, hard-shelled Pas-udeti (dismissively called 'beetles' by Terrans), has never seen Earth and has grown up playing with Pas-udeti children in the city of Karnet, working alongside them on a model spaceport.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: Silvia, a young woman with an inherited gift for summoning vast, alien 'angels' by offering trays of lamb's blood in her family's garden, treats the ritual as a private thrill she has practiced since childhood — she believes herself descended from these beings and destined to eventually join them.

card_summary: # The Collected Stories of Philip K. Dick, Volumes 1-5 *by Philip K.

author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: In the mid-21st century, the Emigration Bureau's interstellar colonization project keeps failing: convicts sent at near-light speed toward Proxima Centauri, reduced to an inch tall to conserve mass, can never regain their lost mass to land safely.

canonical_title: We Can Remember It For You Wholesale
author: Philip K. Dick
date_display: The Magazine of Fantasy & Science Fiction, April 1966
card_summary: Douglas Quail, a clerk at the West Coast Emigration Bureau, wants to have gone to Mars and cannot afford to go.
